articleTitle: Digital Data Protection Using Feistel Network and DNA Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: The growing importance of digital data security has led to increased exploration of advanced cryptographic methods, including innovative bio-inspired techniques such as DNA cryptography. In this paper, we present an enhanced encryption technique that combines a Feistel Network with DNA cryptography. This is achieved by using DNA encoding alongside an R-Box for mapping octal values to RNA codons, integrated with an XOR operation and random round keys. This hybrid approach achieves an impressive avalanche effect of 56 % with just four Feistel rounds, compared to the 53 % achieved by the DES algorithm in 16 rounds. The results highlight the efficiency and robustness of our method in protecting digital information while reducing computational overhead.

articleTitle: Implementing IMS-AKA+: A Solution for Securing Signaling and Media Planes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: Third generation network partnership project pro-posed the main solution for new generation networks, Ip multime-dia subsystem; it is mainly based on Session Initiation Protocol, the main protocol used for signaling. This protocol is a target for several attacks. As such, many improvements to secure Session Initiation Protocol have been proposed, from which we are interested in Ip multimedia subsystem Authentication and Key Agreement+ protocol. To deal with the security of this latter, a two step-verification approach was carried out: in a previous work, security specifications of IMS-AKA+ were described in AVISPA and a logical proof was established showing that IMS-AKA+ resists to many attacks such as man in the middle attack, spoofing attack, to name a few. In this paper, we proceed to the second step of validating IMS-AKA+: an implementation of this protocol was established using OMNET++ in which the functional elements of internet multimedia subsystem and exchanges in-between were specified and described. Furthermore, Ip multimedia subsystem is also based on secure real-time protocol representing the main protocol for data exchange. As such, extending the security to this protocol, we show how to use the keys generated in the signaling plane by IMS-AKA+ protocol. When compared to the standard signaling and media approach using OMNET ++ simulator and Crypto++ cryptography library, our approach outperformed the standard signaling and media planes approach in terms of exchange time.

articleTitle: Towards Efficient Dataset Development: A Case Study of M2Q2+ in Movie QA Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: The development and availability of high-quality datasets are critical to the success of machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Datasets provide the essential foundation for training, validating, and testing models. The need for domain-specific datasets is particularly important in closed-domain systems like Movie NoSQL Question Answering (QA). A well-curated dataset enables models to translate natural language questions into NoSQL queries effectively. This paper introduces an efficient method for developing a tailored dataset for MongoDB-based Movie QA systems. The resulting dataset, M2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>2+, facilitates the translation of natural language questions into MongoDB queries (MQL). The dataset development process includes creating templates, performing data augmentation with the pre-trained T5-base model, and conducting a data revision process to produce the final dataset. A combination of evaluation methods and metrics was applied to ensure that M2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>2+ is high quality.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Approach with Overlapped Classes Aggregation for Intrusion Detection in Internet of Things Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: The rise of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has enhanced several aspects of our lives. However, the dynamic connection between IoT devices, the resource restrictions, and their heterogeneity elevate the risk of network breaches. The intrusion detection system (IDS) is an efficient tool for network traffic investigation. Nevertheless, besides the imbalanced nature of cybersecurity datasets, some also suffer from the class overlap problem. The presence of one of these issues can limit the full potential of the IDS. However, their joining in a dataset drastically degrades its performance when adopting the multi-classification case. Therefore, novel techniques should be explored to handle the attendance of class imbalance with class overlap in cybersecurity datasets. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach with overlapped classes aggregation for intrusion detection enhancement in IoT networks. Each group of overlapped classes is treated as a single class. By doing so, we have eliminated the class overlap and mitigated the class imbalance, resulting in an improved overall performance in exchange for less specification on the type of attack that intruded on the network. In addition, we tackled the remaining imbalance utilizing the class weight technique. The proposed approach surpasses state-of-the-art methods by achieving 88.96% accuracy and high individual detection rates for all the classes on the UNSW-NB15 dataset.

articleTitle: Intelligent Network of Anti-Pollution Stations for Real-Time Prediction and Monitoring of Atmospheric Pollution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: Pollution has a significant impact on public health, particularly for those living in densely populated urban areas affected by industrial and commercial activities. To address this challenge, this paper focuses on the design, development, and prototyping of an Intelligent Network of Anti-Pollution Stations, designed for real-time prediction and monitoring of atmospheric pollution. This network enables the detection of various types of pollution, tracking their geographic spread, predicting emergency situations, and reporting them through real-time monitoring of specific areas. Artificial intelligence plays a key role in enhancing predictive capabilities. Four machine learning algorithms were compared - XGBoost, LightGBM, LSTM, and Random Forest - for predicting the Air Quality Index (AQI), particularly for O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Four Metaheuristic Algorithms for Estimating Parameters in Solar Photovoltaic Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: In the last decade, Metaheuristic Algorithms (MAs) have been widely employed to estimate parameters in photovoltaic (PV) models to maximize solar energy efficiency. This paper presents a comparative study of the performance of four novel and efficient MAs applied to solve the parameter extraction problem in three ubiquitous PV models: the Single-Diode Model (SDM), the Double-Diode Model (DDM), and the Photovoltaic Module Model (PMM). The primary objective of this study is to evaluate and compare the efficiency of these MAs and identify the most effective one based on the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) between the simulated and the actual data. This work compares the performance of the Red-tailed Hawk Optimizer (RTH), the One-to-One Based Optimizer (OOBO), the Sand Cat Swarm Optimization (SCSO), and the Archerfish Hunting Optimizer (AHO). The numerical results demonstrate that RTH significantly outperforms its counterparts in estimating parameters for the examined models. This exceptional performance underscores RTH's efficiency and effectiveness as a powerful tool for parameter estimation in PV models. Given these promising results, RTH stands out as a preferred method and holds the potential for further refinement and enhancement in the future.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Experimental and Computational Methods for Protein Structure Prediction and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: Protein and genetic information are essential in personalizing treatments for individual patients. A major hurdle, however, is the in-depth comprehension of proteins, which is predominantly facilitated by identifying their structures. Accurate prediction and classification of protein structures are crucial for elucidating how proteins operate and interact within biological systems. In bioinformatics, numerous computational methods have been developed to support experimental techniques in protein structure prediction. These approaches draw on diverse data, including protein sequences, genomes, and structural characteristics, while often combining various strategies. This review evaluates the effectiveness of current methods, highlighting their advantages and drawbacks. Additionally, it explores the importance of interdisciplinary collaborations, emphasizing the integration of experimental and computational approaches to showcase how these partnerships can advance the prediction and classification of protein structures.

articleTitle: An Opposition-Based Learning Archerfish Hunting Optimizer for Global Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: This paper introduces OBL-AHO, an enhanced Archerfish Hunting Optimizer (AHO) variant that integrates Opposition-Based Learning (OBL) to improve AHO's exploratory capabilities. By leveraging opposite solutions alongside newly generated ones, OBL-AHO broadens the search space, effectively reducing the risk of local optima entrapment-a common challenge in metaheuristic algorithms. The performance of OBL-AHO is rigorously compared with the original AHO and several prominent Metaheuristic Algorithms (MAs), including TLBO (Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization), PSO (Particle Swarm Optimization), GWO (Grey Wolf Optimizer), OOBO (OnE-to-One Based Optimizer), SSA (Salp Swarm Algorithm). Evaluations were conducted using test functions taken from CEC 2022, and the outcomes were statistically analyzed using the Friedman test. The findings demonstrate that OBL-AHO significantly improves exploration while maintaining competitive exploitation relative to its opponents.

articleTitle: Optimizing Machine Learning for Healthcare Fraud Detection: A Framework Using Hybrid Feature Selection and Hyperparameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: The healthcare insurance sector faces significant challenges due to fraud, leading to substantial financial losses. While machine learning (ML) has shown promise in fraud detection, more advanced methodologies are needed. Feature selection is crucial in enhancing ML model efficiency, balancing accuracy and computational practicality. Healthcare datasets often suffer from imbalanced data, with fraudulent instances being rare. Common techniques like Random Over-Sampling (ROS) and Random Under-Sampling (RUS) have limitations. Additionally, optimal hyperparameter selection is vital for improving ML model accuracy. This paper introduces a new ML framework for healthcare fraud detection, utilizing hybrid feature selection and hyperparameter tuning. It employs algorithms like XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, CatBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Trees, with the tuned Gradient Boosting classifier achieving su-perior results (0.976 accuracy, 0.962 precision, 0.961 recall, 0.962 F1 score, and 0.972 AUC), marking a significant advancement in the field.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving in Agricultural IoT: Intrusion Detection Using Federated Learning and CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: The Agricultural Internet of Things (AIoT) network integrates agriculture with IoT to enhance productivity and improve quality. This infrastructure connects many devices, facilitating extensive information exchange within the network. However, this increased data exchange also heightens the network's susceptibility to attacks and vulnerabilities, posing risks and potentially causing damage to the network infrastructure. Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are effective solutions for detecting attacks and preserving productivity. Many existing approaches in the literature combine deep learning with IDS to create robust anomaly-based IDS. However, these solutions often encounter challenges related to data collection, which compromises user privacy by centralizing data from various entities into a single entity. Our paper proposes a privacy-preserving IDS based on federated learning techniques and Convolutional neural networks (CNN) to develop a robust IDS with significant performance. We evaluate our experiments using a new dataset, Edge-IIoT, which consists of real IoT traffic across binary, 6-class, and 15-class scenarios with 10 and 15 clients. The results demonstrate the performance of our model across all scenarios, achieving 100% and 99.99% accuracy in binary classification and both 6-class and 15-class scenarios, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Head Self-Attention Based Arabic News Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: This paper introduces an Arabic News Recommendation System (ANRS) designed to enhance personalized news recommendations for Arabic-speaking users. By leveraging a multi-head self-attention mechanism, the proposed model effectively captures complex dependencies within Arabic text, addressing challenges posed by the language's rich morphology and contextual nuances. The news encoder uses multi-head self-attention to learn the meaning of Arabic news articles by analyzing interactions between words in titles, body text. Meanwhile, the user encoder models user preferences by examining previously read articles, also using multi-head self-attention to capture connections between articles. Trained on a dataset of Arabic news articles and 15 million user interaction logs, ANRS achieves a high prediction accuracy of 98.6%, significantly outperforming traditional and deep learning-based Arabic recommendation models.

articleTitle: Impact of Deep Learning-Based Entity Recognition on a Feature-Based Entity Linking System: A Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), playing a crucial role in Named Entity Disambiguation (NED), especially when dealing with short texts and queries. Accurate entity identification is essential before linking entities to their corresponding entries in Knowledge Graphs (KGs). This paper presents a novel approach to enhance NED performance in short texts by introducing BERT SocialNER2.0, a state-of-the-art NER model, and integrating it with WeLink, an existing NED system optimized for such texts. Our research provides a comprehensive analysis of the impact of improved NER on NED performance, offering insights into optimizing entity recognition and subsequent linking within KGs. We evaluate our enhanced NED system on several bench-mark datasets, including QALD-5, QALD-7, QALD-8, QALD-9, and LC-QUAD. The results demonstrate consistent performance improvements in entity recognition across these datasets, with cascading benefits for NED tasks, achieving an average F-measure gain of 10% compared to state-of-the-art systems.

articleTitle: FRAME-ArchSoS: A Model-based Framework for the Formal Specification of Reliable Systems of Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: System of Systems (SoS) represents a complex integration of independent and operational constituent systems that interconnect temporarily to achieve overarching objectives. These sub-systems retain a degree of autonomy and can exhibit significant diversity in terms of technology, context, function, and geography. While SoS can provide capabilities that surpass the sum of their constituents, they also introduce challenges related to unpredictability and complexity due to their dynamic and secure behavior. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a multi-level framework that investigates how Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) and formal approaches could be leveraged to model reliable SoS and identify high-impact solutions early in the system development life cycle. This framework, called FRAME-archSoS, comprises (1) an Architectural Description Language (ArchSoS) dedicated to define SoS architectures in a modular and reusable manner, (2) M-SoSRe, a meta model for SoS to identify and represent their reliable scenarios, this step is automated thanks to a generated graphical editor (GE4ArchSoS) to simplify accessibility of people with limited knowledge, (3) a transcription approach from ArchSoS specifications to Maude modules enabling simulation and reconfiguration of SoS behavior while supporting fault tolerance. We illustrate the validity of our proposed framework through an elderly care system (ECG-SoS) example, demonstrating effective complexity management and system integrity.

articleTitle: Advancing Accurate Recognition of Handwritten Arabic Character: An Innovative Hybrid Approach*
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: The Arabic handwriting recognition remains one of the greatest challenges in the field of handwriting recognition. This difficulty arises from the variability of writing styles and the intrinsic complexity of the Arabic language. In our paper, we propose an innovative approach based on hybrid models, combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Support Vector Machines (SVMs), known for their effectiveness in extracting relevant features and their classification quality. A major contribution of our research is the introduction of a majority voting-based classification method. Each CNN-SVM hybrid model “votes” for its prediction, and the class receiving the most votes is selected as the final prediction. Two datasets have been used in this study: the Hijja and AHCD datasets. The results obtained are encouraging. We will also provide a comparative evaluation with existing methods to highlight the advantages and performance of our approach.

articleTitle: Leveraging Pre-trained Transformer Models and Ensemble Learning for Fake News Detection: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: In recent years, the proliferation of fake news has become a major concern due to its potential to influence public opinion, cause panic, and even impact election outcomes. To address this issue, Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques have been proposed as effective solutions. In this study, we present a comprehensive evaluation of transformer-based models, particularly BERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa, alongside ensemble learning techniques, to enhance the performance of fake news detection tasks. Specifically, we fine-tuned these pre-trained models on two widely used datasets: LIAR and ISOT, which represent different levels of complexity in fake news classification. Subsequently, our approach integrates individual transformer models with ensembling methods such as Majority vote, Averaging and Highest-sum, significantly improving classification accuracy. Extensive experiments have been carried out showing that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy in detecting fake news across various standard evaluation metrics, outperforming competitive state-of-the-art baselines.

articleTitle: Enhancing Malware Detection using Deep Learning with SMOTE and Noise-based Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of malware poses a significant security threat to financial institutions, businesses, and individuals. Tackling this growing issue requires innovative methods for the accurate and rapid identification and classification of malware, facilitating comprehensive behavioral analysis. Deep learning has emerged as a powerful tool for malware detection due to its ability to identify complex patterns and anomalies in data. This study investigates the application of a custom-designed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) alongside a hybrid CNN-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, utilizing augmentation techniques for image-based malware classification. The augmentation methods employed include the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and the additive noise. Using the MalImg dataset, the custom-built CNN achieved an impressive classification accuracy of 99.89%, and the hybrid CNN-LSTM model reached 99.68%. Both models outperformed existing state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Earthquake Resilient Management in Northeast Algeria: A Multivariate Time Series Forecasting based on LSTM-Attention Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: Forecasting methods are critical to earthquake management by providing early warning systems and predictive insights into potential hazards. This work proposes a prediction framework for forecasting earthquake magnitude. The methodology involves collecting historical data from the seismic catalog, identifying geophysical characteristics of northeast Algeria, specifically the Sétif (Algeria) region, and proposing a multivariate time series forecasting model based on LSTM with an attention mechanism. The attention neural network learns deeply the most relevant weights representing the subduction zone characteristics that influence earthquake prediction. We validate the proposed model based on real data-sets, and the results show an accurate magnitude forecasting for the northeast Algeria zone.

Author Keywords: Time series forecasting based on LSTM

articleTitle: Extending TOPSIS to Ideal References and Value Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: In this paper, in order to integrate user subjective preferences in MCDM problems, we propose to extend the TOPSIS method to adaptive ideal references and user-imposed constraints expressed in the form of intervals. In this novel method, called TOPSIS*, we design appropriate normalization formulas to incorporate user preferences in order to consistently compute aggregation scores. Consequently, the applicability, precision, and user contentment of TOPSIS is greatly enhanced, rendering it a more effective instrument for decision-making in varied and intricate scenarios. To advocate the benefit of using TOPSIS*, an illustrative example of used car selection is implemented.

articleTitle: Formal Specification and Verification of MQTT Protocol Using CoQ Proof Assistant
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Aspects of Software Engineering (ICAASE)
abstract: Because of its efficiency and lightweight design, the Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol is widely used in Internet of Things (loT) and messaging systems. However, despite its widespread use, guaranteeing the correctness and reliability of MQTT implementations remains a challenge. While model checking has been used to specify and verify properties of MQTT systems, there is a notable absence of formal verification using theorem proving methods such as the Coq proof assistant. This research attempts to fill this gap by formalizing and verifying the MQTT protocol in Coq. This article opens up a new field of study, paving the way for more rigorous verification techniques and enhancing the robustness and reliability of MQTT-based systems through a formalisation of the protocol main concepts and the demonstration of safety properties.
